about.disclaimer: This tool only edits text settings files and never touches the game or its process. Not affiliated with Activision.
app.title: Warzone Config Editor
app.subtitle: Settings editor for Call of Duty: Black Ops 7 / Warzone
backup.title: Backups
backup.restore_confirm: Restore the backup from {time}? The current files are backed up first.
card.technical_key: Original setting name in the game file
card.read_only: Managed by the game - read only
card.new_tooltip: This setting is not in the knowledge base yet; the description comes from the game file.
card.recommended_rule: Recommended value depends on your hardware (optimizer coming soon).
changes.title: Pending changes
checks.note: The check only reads information - it never changes your system or BIOS.
checks.expo.title: Memory profile (EXPO/XMP)
checks.expo.problem: RAM runs at {speed} MT/s although the modules are rated {rated} MT/s - the {profile} profile is not enabled.
checks.expo.fix: Enable the {profile} profile in BIOS/UEFI (Gigabyte: Extreme Memory Profile, ASUS: AI Overclock Tuner, MSI: A-XMP/EXPO, ASRock: DRAM Profile). On Ryzen 7000/9000, 6000 MT/s with UCLK=MEMCLK (1:1) is the usual sweet spot. Faster RAM improves 1% lows in CPU-bound games like Warzone.
checks.expo.ok: Memory runs with an overclocking profile ({speed} MT/s).
checks.channels.title: Dual-channel memory
checks.channels.problem: All memory sits in one channel - memory bandwidth is halved.
checks.channels.fix: Use two modules in the slots named in the motherboard manual (usually A2 and B2 - the 2nd and 4th slot from the CPU).
checks.ram_size.title: Amount of RAM
checks.ram_size.problem: {gb} GB installed - Warzone needs at least {min} GB.
checks.ram_size.fix: Add RAM as two identical modules (e.g. 2 x 16 GB).
checks.game_drive.title: Game drive
checks.game_drive.problem_hdd: The game is on a hard disk ({letter}:) - expect long loading and textures popping in late.
checks.game_drive.problem_sata: The game is on a SATA SSD ({letter}:) although a faster NVMe drive is available.
checks.game_drive.fix: Move it in Steam (Properties → Installed Files → Move install folder) or Battle.net (Settings → Game Install/Update).
checks.game_drive.ok: The game is on a fast drive ({letter}:).
checks.disk_space.title: Free space on the game drive
checks.disk_space.problem: Only {gb} GB free - updates and the shader cache need room (keep {min} GB+).
checks.disk_space.fix: Free some space or move the game to a bigger drive.
checks.refresh.title: Monitor refresh rate
checks.refresh.problem: Windows runs the monitor at {hz} Hz, but it supports {max} Hz.
checks.refresh.fix: Settings → System → Display → Advanced display → Choose a refresh rate: {max} Hz.
checks.refresh.ok: The monitor runs at its maximum of {hz} Hz.
checks.driver.title: Graphics driver
checks.driver.problem: Driver {installed} is older than {recommended}, which the game recommends.
checks.driver.fix: Install the latest Game Ready driver (NVIDIA App or nvidia.com).
checks.pcie.title: Graphics card slot (PCIe)
checks.pcie.problem: The card uses {width} PCIe lanes instead of {width_max} - wrong slot, riser cable or BIOS setting.
checks.pcie.fix: Put the card in the top x16 slot and check riser cables and PCIe settings in BIOS.
checks.rebar.title: Resizable BAR
checks.rebar.problem_heaps: Resizable BAR is off, but the game setting GPU Upload Heaps is on - it only helps with ReBAR.
checks.rebar.fix: Enable 'Above 4G Decoding' and 'Re-Size BAR' in BIOS. Until then turn GPU Upload Heaps off.
checks.power_plan.title: Power plan
checks.power_plan.problem: The Power saver plan lowers CPU clocks while gaming.
checks.power_plan.fix: Settings → System → Power → Power mode: Best performance (with the Balanced plan). On dual-CCD X3D processors keep the Balanced plan; on others High performance is fine too.
checks.power_plan.ok: A performance power plan is active.
checks.hags.title: Hardware-accelerated GPU scheduling
checks.hags.problem: HAGS is off - DLSS Frame Generation needs it.
checks.hags.fix: Settings → System → Display → Graphics → Advanced settings → On, then restart.
checks.game_mode.title: Game Mode
checks.recording.title: Background recording
checks.recording.problem: Xbox Game Bar records gameplay in the background, which costs some performance.
checks.recording.fix: Settings → Gaming → Captures → turn off 'Record what happened'.
checks.hvci.title: Memory integrity (HVCI)
checks.hvci.problem: Memory integrity is on - better security, but it can cost a few % FPS. Your choice.
checks.hvci.fix: Windows Security → Device security → Core isolation. Keep it on if security matters more.
checks.igpu.title: Integrated graphics
checks.igpu.problem: Your PC also has integrated graphics; the game uses {game_gpu}.
checks.igpu.problem_wrong: The game is set to use {game_gpu} instead of {dedicated}!
checks.igpu.fix: Choose the dedicated card in the game (Display → Graphics card) or set Call of Duty to High performance in Settings → Display → Graphics.
tweaks.confirm_note: Only this setting of your Windows account changes. The previous value is saved - 'Restore' in this tab puts it back. No administrator rights are needed.
tweaks.game_mode_on.title: Turn on Game Mode
tweaks.game_mode_on.confirm: Game Mode will be turned on (Settings → Gaming → Game Mode).
tweaks.recording_off.title: Turn off background recording
tweaks.recording_off.confirm: Xbox Game Bar will stop recording gameplay in the background ('Record what happened'). Recording on demand (Win+Alt+R) still works.
tweaks.auto_hdr_off.title: Turn off Auto HDR
tweaks.auto_hdr_off.confirm: Auto HDR will be turned off for all games. The HDR option in the game's own settings is not affected.
tweaks.gpu_high_performance.title: High-performance GPU for Call of Duty
tweaks.gpu_high_performance.confirm: Windows will always run cod.exe on the high-performance (dedicated) graphics card. Takes effect the next time the game starts.
tweaks.fso_default.title: Default fullscreen optimizations for cod.exe
tweaks.fso_default.confirm: The 'Disable fullscreen optimizations' tick will be removed from cod.exe; other compatibility options stay.
tweaks.mouse_accel_off.title: Turn off mouse acceleration
tweaks.mouse_accel_off.confirm: 'Enhance pointer precision' will be turned off. It takes effect immediately - the pointer on the desktop will move a little differently.
tweaks.power_balanced.title: Balanced power plan
tweaks.power_balanced.confirm: The power plan will switch to Balanced, as AMD recommends for dual-CCD Ryzen X3D processors.
tweaks.power_best_performance.title: Balanced plan + Best performance
tweaks.power_best_performance.confirm: The power plan will switch to Balanced and the power mode to 'Best performance' (Settings → System → Power).
win.note: Read without administrator rights. The app changes a setting only when you click 'Fix' and confirm - always restorable. Other rows open the right Windows page or explain what to do. Each row shows how strong the evidence is: many popular 'tweaks' do nothing.
win.refresh_tip: Read the settings again (e.g. after changing something in Windows).
win.impact.required_tip: Without it the game blocks Ranked and some playlists (Ricochet anti-cheat).
win.impact.proven_tip: Benchmarks or the hardware vendor confirm a real effect.
win.impact.situational_tip: Helps on some PCs or setups; the evidence is mixed.
win.impact.none_tip: Worth knowing, but it does not change how Call of Duty runs.
win.myths_title: Myths - not worth it or harmful
win.myths_note: Popular Windows 'gaming tweaks' that tests show do nothing on Windows 11 - or break something. If one of them is already set, consider restoring the default.
win.bios_note: Windows cannot read BIOS settings; what it can see indirectly is in the rows above. Menu names differ between vendors (Gigabyte / ASUS / MSI / ASRock).
win.bios.expo.title: Memory profile (EXPO / XMP)
win.bios.expo.text: Turn on EXPO (AMD) or XMP (Intel). Gigabyte: Extreme Memory Profile, ASUS: AI Overclock Tuner, MSI: A-XMP / EXPO, ASRock: DRAM Profile.
win.bios.rebar.title: Resizable BAR
win.bios.rebar.text: Above 4G Decoding: Enabled and Re-Size BAR Support: Enabled / Auto (needs CSM off).
win.bios.secure_boot.title: CSM and Secure Boot
win.bios.secure_boot.text: CSM: Disabled, Secure Boot: Enabled, keys: 'Install default keys'. Required by the game.
win.bios.tpm.title: Firmware TPM
win.bios.tpm.text: AMD: 'AMD CPU fTPM' (or 'Security Device Support'), Intel: 'Intel Platform Trust Technology (PTT)': Enabled. Required by the game.
win.bios.svm.title: CPU virtualization (SVM / VT-x)
win.bios.svm.text: AMD: 'SVM Mode', Intel: 'Intel Virtualization Technology'. You can leave it on - it costs nothing by itself, and WSL2 / Docker need it.
win.bios.pbo.title: PBO, Curve Optimizer, C-states
win.bios.pbo.text: Leave them on Auto unless you test stability yourself - an unstable undervolt causes crashes that look like game bugs.
win.bios.intel_profile.title: Intel 13th/14th gen: power profile
win.bios.intel_profile.text: Choose 'Intel Default Settings' (the Intel Baseline / Performance profile) and keep the BIOS up to date - it contains the 0x12B microcode.
checks.secure_boot.title: Secure Boot
checks.secure_boot.problem: Secure Boot is off - Black Ops 7 and Warzone require it (together with TPM 2.0). Without it you lose Ranked and most playlists.
checks.secure_boot.fix: In BIOS/UEFI: Boot → CSM: Disabled, then Security/Boot → Secure Boot: Enabled and 'Install default keys'. The system disk must be GPT (see 'Boot mode'). Activision's Secure Attestation Wizard (in the game folder) shows what is still missing.
checks.boot_mode.title: Boot mode (UEFI + GPT)
checks.boot_mode.problem_legacy: Windows boots in Legacy/CSM mode - Secure Boot (required by the game) only works in UEFI mode.
checks.boot_mode.problem_mbr: The system disk uses MBR - UEFI with Secure Boot needs a GPT disk.
checks.boot_mode.fix: Convert the disk without losing data: as administrator run 'mbr2gpt /validate /allowFullOS', then 'mbr2gpt /convert /allowFullOS' (suspend BitLocker first). Then switch BIOS to UEFI (CSM: Disabled) and enable Secure Boot. Make a backup before you start.
checks.tpm.title: TPM 2.0
checks.tpm.problem_missing: No TPM found - the game requires TPM 2.0.
checks.tpm.problem_old: TPM {version} found - the game requires TPM 2.0.
checks.tpm.problem_firmware: {device} firmware {firmware} is known to fail the game's attestation.
checks.tpm.fix: Enable the firmware TPM in BIOS (AMD: 'AMD CPU fTPM', Intel: 'Intel Platform Trust Technology (PTT)') or update the BIOS - new versions also bring fixed TPM firmware.
checks.uac.title: User Account Control (UAC)
checks.uac.problem: UAC is set to 'Never notify'. The game's security components (CODBrokerInstaller, enrollaik) need a UAC prompt that you accept - otherwise attestation fails.
checks.uac.fix: Start → 'Change User Account Control settings' → move the slider back to the default level (second from the top).
checks.secure_boot_certs.title: Secure Boot certificates (2023)
checks.secure_boot_certs.problem: The 2023 Secure Boot certificates are not installed yet (status: {status}). The 2011 certificates expire in 2026 - the PC keeps booting, but stops getting boot-level security updates.
checks.secure_boot_certs.fix: Install all Windows updates and restart. If the status does not change, update the motherboard BIOS.
checks.input_remap.title: Input remapping tools
checks.input_remap.problem: Running: {apps}. Ricochet detects input remapping and devices like Cronus Zen / XIM - you risk a ban.
checks.input_remap.fix: Close it (and its service) before launching the game, or uninstall it.
checks.virtualization.title: Virtualization (hypervisor)
checks.virtualization.problem_no_svm: Installed: {features}, but CPU virtualization (SVM / VT-x) is off in BIOS, so they cannot start. No cost while gaming - but WSL2, Docker and virtual machines will not work.
checks.virtualization.problem_features: The Windows hypervisor runs for: {features}. In CPU-bound games it costs a few % FPS, similar to VBS.
checks.virtualization.fix: If you don't use WSL, Docker or virtual machines, turn these features off: Optional features → More Windows features (restart needed). If you use them, leave it - the cost is small. Without them, the SVM / VT-x switch in BIOS itself costs nothing.
checks.virtualization.ok: No hypervisor is running - no virtualization cost.
checks.virtualization.ok_vbs: The hypervisor runs only for Windows security (VBS).
checks.antivirus.title: Antivirus
checks.antivirus.problem_outdated: Antivirus definitions are out of date ({names}).
checks.antivirus.fix: Turn on real-time protection in Windows Security or in your antivirus and update it. Never turn it off for performance - if loading stutters, add only the game folder to the exclusions.
checks.antivirus.ok_third_party: Active: {names} (Windows Defender in passive mode - that is normal). If loading stutters, add the game folder to the exclusions in {names}, not in Defender.
checks.driver_blocklist.title: Vulnerable driver blocklist
checks.driver_blocklist.problem: The Microsoft vulnerable driver blocklist is off.
checks.driver_blocklist.fix: Windows Security → Device security → Core isolation details → Microsoft Vulnerable Driver Blocklist: On.
checks.winring0.title: WinRing0 driver
checks.winring0.problem: An old WinRing0 driver is installed ({drivers}). Defender flags it as HackTool - it gives any program access to the hardware.
checks.winring0.fix: Update or remove the tool that installed it (old MSI Afterburner, OpenRGB, FanControl, HWiNFO, Libre Hardware Monitor…). Current versions no longer use WinRing0.
checks.gpu_preference.title: Graphics card for the game
checks.gpu_preference.problem: Windows decides which GPU runs Call of Duty. On PCs with integrated graphics it is safer to choose the dedicated card.
checks.gpu_preference.problem_power_savi: Windows is set to run Call of Duty on the power-saving (integrated) GPU!
checks.gpu_preference.fix: Settings → System → Display → Graphics → Call of Duty (cod.exe) → High performance.
checks.gpu_preference.ok: Call of Duty is set to High performance.
checks.auto_hdr.title: Auto HDR
checks.auto_hdr.problem: Auto HDR is on. Call of Duty has its own HDR, so Auto HDR adds nothing here - and in other games it takes some GPU time.
checks.auto_hdr.fix: Settings → System → Display → HDR → Auto HDR: Off. Use the game's own HDR option instead.
checks.mpo.title: Multiplane overlay (MPO)
checks.mpo.problem: MPO is disabled by a registry tweak (OverlayTestMode = 5). It is a fix for flicker and black screens on some PCs; on Windows 11 24H2+ it is often ignored or causes video stutter.
checks.mpo.fix: If there were no flicker problems, restore the default with NVIDIA's mpo_restore.reg file and restart the PC.
checks.fso.title: Fullscreen optimizations (cod.exe)
checks.fso.problem: 'Disable fullscreen optimizations' is ticked for cod.exe. It only affects old DirectX 9-11 games - Call of Duty uses DirectX 12, so it changes nothing. You can leave it.
checks.game_bar.title: Xbox Game Bar
checks.game_bar.problem: Xbox Game Bar is not installed (often removed by 'debloat' scripts). Windows uses it to recognise games for Game Mode.
checks.game_bar.problem_x3d: Xbox Game Bar is not installed - on a dual-CCD Ryzen X3D the AMD driver needs it to move the game onto the V-Cache cores.
checks.game_bar.fix: Install 'Xbox Game Bar' from the Microsoft Store. You don't have to use it - background recording can stay off.
checks.power_plan.problem_mode: Balanced plan without the 'Best performance' power mode - the CPU may clock down between frames.
checks.power_plan.problem_x3d: A dual-CCD Ryzen X3D needs the Balanced plan. With High or Ultimate performance the AMD driver cannot park the CCD without V-Cache, and the game may run on the slower cores.
checks.power_plan.ok_mode: Balanced plan with the 'Best performance' power mode.
checks.power_plan.ok_x3d: Balanced plan - as AMD recommends for dual-CCD X3D.
checks.processor_state.title: Processor power limits
checks.processor_state.problem_max: The active power plan caps the CPU at {max}% - it never reaches full clocks.
checks.processor_state.problem_min: The High performance plan was edited: the minimum processor state is {min}% (default 100%). It works, but it is no longer the stock plan.
checks.processor_state.fix: Control Panel → Power Options → Change plan settings → Change advanced power settings → Restore plan defaults (or Processor power management → set the value).
checks.x3d_driver.title: AMD 3D V-Cache driver
checks.x3d_driver.problem_missing: The 'AMD 3D V-Cache Performance Optimizer' service is missing - without it a dual-CCD X3D may run the game on the CCD without V-Cache.
checks.x3d_driver.problem_stopped: The 'AMD 3D V-Cache Performance Optimizer' service is not running.
checks.x3d_driver.fix: Install the latest AMD chipset driver for your motherboard (amd.com → Chipsets) and restart.
checks.x3d_driver.ok: The AMD 3D V-Cache service is running.
checks.core_parking.title: Core parking
checks.core_parking.problem: Core parking is disabled in the power plan - on a dual-CCD X3D the AMD driver needs it to park the CCD without V-Cache while you play.
checks.core_parking.fix: Use the stock Balanced plan (restore plan defaults) and don't use 'unpark cores' tools.
checks.intel_microcode.title: Intel microcode (13th/14th gen)
checks.intel_microcode.problem: Microcode {revision} is older than {required} - 13th/14th gen Core CPUs without it can degrade and crash.
checks.intel_microcode.fix: Update the motherboard BIOS (the microcode comes with it) and use the 'Intel Default Settings' profile.
checks.windows_version.title: Windows version
checks.windows_version.problem_win10: Windows 10 (build {build}) no longer gets security updates.
checks.windows_version.problem_amd: Windows {version} ({build}) lacks the branch-prediction fix for Ryzen 5000/7000/9000 - 24H2 and newer give about 10% more FPS on average.
checks.windows_version.problem_arrow_lak: Core Ultra 200S processors need build 26100.2161 or newer (and a current BIOS) - without the fix Intel measured 6-30% lower performance.
checks.windows_version.fix: Settings → Windows Update → install all updates (or the 24H2 / 25H2 feature update).
checks.nvidia_hotfix.title: NVIDIA driver after the October 2025 update
checks.nvidia_hotfix.problem: Windows update KB5066835 slows down some games on NVIDIA cards with driver {installed}; driver {required} or newer fixes it.
checks.nvidia_hotfix.fix: Install the latest Game Ready driver (NVIDIA App or nvidia.com).
checks.reboot_pending.title: Restart pending
checks.reboot_pending.problem: Windows is waiting for a restart to finish installing updates - update work in the background can cause stutter.
checks.pagefile.title: Page file
checks.pagefile.problem_off: The page file is disabled - Call of Duty then crashes with memory errors, even with plenty of RAM.
checks.pagefile.problem_small: The page file is only {gb} GB - too small for Call of Duty, which can crash with memory errors.
checks.pagefile.fix: System Properties → Advanced → Performance: Settings → Advanced → Virtual memory: Change → 'Automatically manage paging file size'.
checks.pagefile.ok_auto: Windows manages the page file size.
checks.system_drive_space.title: Free space on the system drive
checks.system_drive_space.problem: Only {gb} GB free on {letter}: - the page file, updates and the DirectX shader cache need room.
checks.system_drive_space.fix: Settings → System → Storage → Cleanup recommendations. Don't delete the DirectX Shader Cache - it rebuilds with stutter.
checks.trim.title: TRIM for SSDs
checks.trim.problem: TRIM is disabled - SSDs slow down over time without it.
checks.overlays.title: Overlays in the background
checks.overlays.problem: Programs that can draw over the game ({count}): {apps}. Each overlay hooks into rendering and can add stutter or latency.
checks.overlays.fix: Keep one overlay at most: turn off the in-game overlay in the others (Discord: Settings → Game Overlay, Steam: game Properties → General, NVIDIA App: Settings). For an FPS cap, the game's own limiter or NVIDIA Reflex is better than RTSS.
checks.overlays.ok: At most one overlay app is running.
checks.mouse_acceleration.title: Mouse acceleration
checks.mouse_acceleration.problem: 'Enhance pointer precision' is on. The game uses raw input, so aiming is not affected - but menus and the desktop move differently from the game.
checks.mouse_acceleration.fix: Settings → Bluetooth & devices → Mouse → Additional mouse settings → Pointer Options → untick 'Enhance pointer precision'.
checks.network.title: Network connection
checks.network.problem_wifi: You play over Wi-Fi - ping and packet loss vary more than on a cable.
checks.network.fix: Use an Ethernet cable if you can.
myths.hpet.title: Forcing HPET (bcdedit useplatformclock)
myths.hpet.why: No measurable gain; forcing the platform clock can even add latency. If it is set, remove it ('bcdedit /deletevalue useplatformclock').
myths.timer_resolution.title: Timer resolution tools
myths.timer_resolution.why: Since Windows 10 2004 the timer resolution is set per process, and Windows 11 ignores it for hidden windows. The game sets what it needs itself.
myths.nagle.title: Disabling Nagle's algorithm (TcpNoDelay, TcpAckFrequency)
myths.nagle.why: These settings affect TCP only - Call of Duty gameplay traffic uses UDP.
myths.core_parking.title: Disabling core parking
myths.core_parking.why: No benchmark shows a gain on Windows 11, and on dual-CCD Ryzen X3D it breaks moving the game onto the V-Cache cores.
myths.ultimate_plan.title: 'Ultimate Performance' or custom 'gaming' power plans
myths.ultimate_plan.why: No measured gain over High performance or Balanced with 'Best performance'; more heat and power draw at idle. Harmful on dual-CCD X3D.
myths.services.title: Disabling SysMain, search indexing or Fast Startup
myths.services.why: Game benchmarks show no difference on an SSD with enough RAM - you only lose features.
myths.pagefile_off.title: Turning off the page file
myths.pagefile_off.why: Call of Duty crashes with memory errors without it, even with 32-64 GB of RAM.
myths.usb_suspend.title: Disabling USB selective suspend
myths.usb_suspend.why: A mouse in use is never suspended; the claimed 2-5 ms gains have never been measured.
myths.nvme_driver.title: Forcing the new native NVMe driver
myths.nvme_driver.why: An experiment: faster in synthetic tests, no gain in games, breaks SSD tools and can trigger BitLocker recovery. Microsoft has blocked the trick.
myths.debloat.title: 'Debloat' scripts that remove Xbox components
myths.debloat.why: Removing Xbox Game Bar breaks game detection for Game Mode and the AMD X3D driver; such scripts also change many settings at once with no easy way back.
myths.security_off.title: Turning off Defender, Smart App Control or Secure Boot
myths.security_off.why: No measured FPS gain. Secure Boot is required by the game, and Smart App Control may not turn back on without reinstalling Windows.

error.readonly: Could not change the read-only attribute: {error}

history.title: History
history.empty: No history yet. Entries appear when you save or when the game changes the file.
history.undo_entry_tip: Puts back the values from before this entry - only for the settings listed.
history.restore_state_tip: Loads every setting exactly as it was right after this entry.
history.applied: {count} setting(s) loaded into the editor - review them and save to apply.
history.nothing_to_apply: Nothing to restore - the values already match.
hw.title: Your hardware
impact.title: Impact
notice.game_changed: The game changed {count} setting(s) since the editor last saw this file: {names}.
notice.undone: Values from before the game's changes are back in the editor - save to apply them.
optimizer.title: Optimize settings
optimizer.bottleneck_hint: Check it in game: Settings → Interface → Telemetry → turn on GPU time and CPU time. In a match, the larger time is your bottleneck (1080p/1440p is usually CPU, 4K usually GPU).
optimizer.summary: {changes} recommended change(s) for your PC · {unchanged} already optimal · {skipped} skipped
optimizer.nothing: Your settings already match these recommendations.
optimizer.applied: Applied {count} optimized setting(s) - review and save.
optimizer.system_hint: Fix first - it matters more than game settings: {items}. See System check.
page.empty_filtered: Nothing to show with the current filters.
preset.not_applicable: {count} recommendation(s) do not apply to this file or GPU.
readonly.explain: Read-only files stop game updates from resetting your settings, but the game also cannot save changes made in its own menu. Unlock before changing settings in the game.
reset.recommended_text: On next start the game will reset ALL settings to its recommended values. Continue?
reset.not_available: This file has no RecommendedSet setting.
save.confirm_text: Write {count} change(s) to both slots? A backup of the current files is made first.
save.success: Settings saved. Start the game to use them.
save.game_running_text: Close the game completely before saving - it rewrites the settings files when it exits and would undo your changes.
save.read_only_note: The files were read-only and stay read-only after saving.
save.disk_changed: The file was changed on disk after you opened it (probably by the game). Saving overwrites those changes - they will stay available in History. Save anyway?
save.failed: Saving failed: {error}. The previous files were restored.
share.title: Share settings
share.note: Never included: audio device ids, window position, detected hardware, driver versions, file paths or account ids. Nothing is sent anywhere - you copy or save the text yourself.
share.unsaved: The export includes your unsaved changes.
spec.title: Hardware & system
spec.profile_off: off - running at the default JEDEC speed
status.changed_on_disk: The file was changed outside the editor (probably by the game).
status.changed_on_disk_dirty: The file changed on disk (probably the game). Use Reload to see it - your unsaved changes will be lost.
status.discarded: All changes discarded - Ctrl+Z brings them back.
status.game_reset: On next start the game will reset all settings to its recommendations - save first.
templates.title: Templates & presets
templates.user_empty: No templates yet - create one from your current settings.
templates.nothing_to_change: Your current settings already match this template.
templates.info_hardware_note: Hardware-specific values (GPU, monitor, audio devices, window, detected hardware) are never saved in templates.
templates.applied: Applied {count} setting(s) from "{name}" - review and save.
tools.game_reset: Let the game reset all settings…
unsaved.title: Unsaved changes
unsaved.text: You have {count} unsaved change(s). Save them first?
